reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that thermal aging at 700°C causes impurity-driven phase segregation and softening in a single-phase RHEA, but it does not address the effect of simultaneous mechanical loading, stress-assisted diffusion, or the specific link to brittle fracture and toughness loss. The hypothesis extends the thermal aging findings to a combined stress-temperature regime without direct supporting evidence for the mechanical component.
premises: Stress-assisted diffusion of interstitial impurities (O, N) occurs under demanding mechanical loading at elevated temperatures.
This impurity mobility leads to localized solute segregation at grain boundaries and dislocations.
Segregation promotes nucleation of brittle intermetallic precipitates or second phases.
Formation of these brittle phases interrupts plastic flow and causes a loss of toughness or brittle fracture.
The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that thermal aging alone at 700°C causes impurity-driven phase segregation and softening in a single-phase RHEA.
